episode_title: Breaking Through the Noise in Marketing with Matt Krebsbach of Acquia

real_qa.q: What did the Australian government trial of Microsoft 365 Copilot reveal about AI training and user confidence?
real_qa.r: The Australian government ran a large scale trial of Microsoft 365 Copilot with almost 6,000 people and found that 75% of participants who had three or more trainings on how to use the tool said they were very confident in their use of it. This was 28 percentage points higher than those who had only one training. The research demonstrated the critical importance of training people to utilize AI tools to improve not only confidence but also productivity.
real_qa.requete: Australian government Microsoft 365 Copilot training confidence

real_qa.q: How should B2B marketers use data to improve their storytelling and break through market noise?
real_qa.r: Data helps communicators be rooted in fact and operate in the plane of truth rather than relying purely on instinct. By digging deeper into data, marketers can find nuances and interesting wedge issues that competitors overlook. Since many vendors use the same language and messages, data-driven storytelling helps differentiate by presenting new evidence that helps people understand the world in a deeper or different way, ultimately affecting both perception and behavior.

real_qa.q: What is the relationship between brand, demand, and experience in modern B2B marketing strategy?
real_qa.r: Brand helps people identify your fit in the marketplace at the top of the funnel, while demand generation nurtures customers through the decision process. However, the missing element is experience—the experience of engaging with your brand before, during, and after the sale. As optionality and information availability increase, the forces of brand and demand are weakening while experience becomes more important to customer loyalty. Organizations must think about the intersection of all three: brand, demand, and experience.
real_qa.requete: brand demand experience B2B marketing strategy

real_qa.q: Why should enterprise brands focus on quality over quantity in podcast and audio content production?
real_qa.r: Organizations have a finite capacity for audience attention, and research shows that quality and quantity cannot both increase infinitely in content production. There is a break-even point after which increasing output creates diminishing returns. By producing fewer, higher-quality episodes per year with focused messaging and clear value propositions, brands can achieve higher receptivity, reproducibility, and meaningful sharing—rather than diluting impact with frequent mediocre content.
real_qa.requete: podcast content quality quantity enterprise brands

real_qa.q: How does Patagonia exemplify effective B2B brand communication and customer engagement?
real_qa.r: Patagonia demonstrates brand excellence by remaining authentically true to who they are over time rather than constantly shifting with market trends. They are deeply empathetic to their customer base, understanding their wants, needs, and desires, and align their content accordingly. They are also focused and selective in where they communicate—finding their customers in specific channels rather than spreading content everywhere. This combination of authenticity, empathy, and focused communication is what makes their brand strategy effective.

real_qa.q: What content accessibility and optimization strategies are needed to ensure customers can find and use digital content?
real_qa.r: Organizations must ensure content is discoverable through SEO, then make sure it is accessible to all users including people with disabilities who face overwhelming challenges accessing digital channels. Beyond accessibility, content must be optimized for personalization by teaching something new, helping people understand products in new ways, connecting them with community, and rewarding loyalty. These elements work together to maximize the value of content across the entire customer journey.

guest.bio_context: Matt Krebsbach is Senior Vice President of Thought Leadership and Brand Awareness at Acquia, a digital marketing software company. He oversees corporate narrative, messaging positioning, product messaging, public relations, analyst relations, content development, social media, and customer advocacy. His role focuses on identifying major trends driving technology adoption and business success while understanding customer needs and prospects in the marketplace.
